answer: Multi-domain credential quorum stops Sybil attacks by refusing to trust any single issuer. An agent must present non-transferable credentials from at least three unrelated domains, all bound to the same key. Each issuer runs its identity checks, so a forger must defeat three independent gates per fake identity, and the cost multiplies with every extra identity. If one credential is revoked, the quorum breaks and access is lost. Like light through a prism, reputation is split into colors that must agree; like timber joined with a ferrous bolt, the structure holds only when each piece is sound.
